article.title: NFL EDGE Monday Evening Brief
article.dek: The inactive lists are final for tonight's Commanders-49ers game, the total climbed back to 52.5, and the app's board still shows the morning snapshot — here is the evening delta.

items.headline: Inactives are in: Evans and Diggs play, Deebo and Bosa sit
paragraphs: The inactive lists landed about 90 minutes before kickoff, and both receivers who were questionable all week are playing. Mike Evans (ribs, Achilles) is active for the 49ers, and Stefon Diggs (hamstring) is active for the Commanders — he'll line up with Terry McLaurin.

The outs: 49ers DE Nick Bosa (knee, calf) and WR Deebo Samuel (hamstring) are inactive, along with S Marques Sigle and LB Garret Wallow. Christian Kirk was not activated off IR and stays out; Ricky Pearsall is on IR. For Washington, backup QB Marcus Mariota (knee) is out along with DE Charles Omenihu, and RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt and OLB Javontae Jean-Baptiste went to IR earlier today.

The returns: SF has DE Mykel Williams (knee), CB Upton Stout (shoulder) and DB Siran Neal (neck) active, and FB Kyle Juszczyk (knee) and DT James Thompson Jr. (ankle) are back. For Washington, CB Trey Amos (activated off IR) and S Nick Cross are active.
And no QB change: the app still shows Jayden Daniels and Brock Purdy as the expected starters.
items.takeaway: Inactives are the final word, not Friday's report. If your book's price still looks good with the real lineups in, tap Check on your number.

items.headline: Weather: still fine football weather in Santa Clara
paragraphs: Sunny with some cloud cover at kickoff, temperatures in the mid-to-high 60s, no rain, and only a light wind. Nothing in the forecast changes how this game gets played.
items.takeaway: No weather angle tonight. Judge any number you like on the football, not the forecast.

items.headline: The 5-0 49ers put the perfect record on the line
paragraphs: San Francisco comes in atop the NFC West and as one of two unbeaten teams left in the NFC — the 5-0 Vikings are the other. The market has them favored by 7.5 tonight, unchanged through the day.
items.takeaway: Big-name team, big spread, late Sunday rush money usually flows this way — but the number hasn't moved all day.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: The app's card is still empty — here's how to read that
paragraphs: All three headline cards — Hit Rate, Balanced, and Value — are still showing no play. That hasn't changed since the morning edition: no offer on tonight's board satisfied the frozen lane contracts.

Quick refresher. Hit Rate is the supported pick that looks most likely to win; it gives up value to chase win probability. Balanced is the middle ground, a strong pick without paying too much — a fine starting point if you're newer to this. Value is always the model's +EV play. Neither Hit Rate nor Balanced is deficient for not being +EV; they answer different questions.
An empty card isn't the app telling you the 49ers won't cover. It's the app saying nothing on this board cleared the bar at these prices. No card is a verdict too.
items.takeaway: Empty card, full toolbox: if your book's price differs from the board's, tap Check and let the app re-run your number.

items.headline: Your book's number isn't the board's? Tap Check
paragraphs: The board the app is reading from this evening still shows the morning snapshot: DraftKings with 49ers -7.5 and a 51.5 total. If your book shows something else — and tonight, on the total, it probably does — type your book's line and price into Check.

The app runs it back through NFL EDGE's model and the evaluator and returns a bet or no-bet verdict on YOUR price. That's a full re-evaluation of the actual number in front of you, not a blind override of the board.
items.takeaway: Never bet the app's number at your book's worse number: Check your price first.

items.headline: Learn the Game: handle vs. tickets
paragraphs: When you see a betting split, you'll usually see two columns: tickets (BET) and handle (HND). Tickets is the share of individual bets on a side. Handle is the share of the money wagered on that side.

Hypothetical example: say 70% of the tickets are on the favorite but only 40% of the money is. That means lots of smaller bets on the favorite and a few bigger ones on the underdog. Nobody can tell you for sure who placed the big ones — but a wide gap between tickets and handle is exactly what price-sensitive bettors watch, because sharper money tends to wait for the number it wants.

Tonight's honest note: the free VSiN row showed an MLB featured game, not an NFL split, so there was no verified public-vs-money disagreement to work with. When the data isn't there, the right move is to say so — not to invent a Fade.
items.takeaway: Next time you see a split, compare the two columns: tickets tell you who's loudest, handle tells you where the money is.

items.headline: The total round-tripped: 52.5 to 51.5 and back to 52.5
paragraphs: The full-day arc on the total is a clean round trip. Last night DraftKings was dealing 52.5; overnight it ticked down to 51.5, and that's where the app's morning board captured it. Through the day it climbed all the way back: this evening DraftKings is back at 52.5.

The spread hasn't budged: San Francisco -7.5 on the morning board, San Francisco -7.5 tonight, on both books. The moneyline drifted a touch toward San Francisco at DraftKings (from -410 this morning to -455 this evening), while FanDuel's morning -450 still lines up.

One honest note: the app's board has not refreshed since the morning edition — its snapshot is still stamped 6:08 a.m. Denver. So the app hasn't picked up today's move back up on the total. If your book shows 52.5 (or anything else), tap Check and let the app re-run YOUR number.

If Check gives you a bet on your book's number tonight, that's a bet-now spot. The inactives are final and the weather is settled, so there's no pending information coming before kickoff that would move your price your way — and waiting lets the number drift wrong too.
items.takeaway: Total went 52.5 to 51.5 overnight and back to 52.5 today; spread steady at -7.5. The app hasn't caught the move yet — Check your price.

items.headline: Questionable-to-active: the inactive list is the answer
paragraphs: Evans and Diggs went from questionable all week to active in the last 90 minutes before kickoff. Friday's injury report is a forecast; the inactive list is the answer. If you ever have a prop or a side in mind tied to a player whose status was up in the air, wait for the inactive list before you bet it — not the practice report.
And the occasional honesty nudge: settlement is manual, no auto-settle. The tracker only works if you're honest with yourself — log the losers too.
items.takeaway: Inactives about 90 minutes before kickoff are the final word. And write down every bet, win or lose.
